summary: Namco's cover-pedal light-gun shooter series, including main arcade entries, GunCon console ports, Crisis Zone, Razing Storm, and mobile spin-offs.

entries.title: Time Crisis
entries.definitive_edition: Arcade original plus PlayStation Special mode supplement

emulation.emulator: Arcade hardware/emulation / DuckStation for Special mode
emulation.notes: Use arcade-style pedal/gun input where possible; use DuckStation for the PlayStation supplement.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Arcade cabinet fidelity plus high-resolution PS1 supplement

primary.version: Original Namco Super System 22 arcade release
primary.why: The first Time Crisis was designed around the arcade light gun and foot pedal. The PlayStation port adds Special mode stages, but it also has cut frame rate/polygon compromises and no arcade blowback, so the arcade version remains the highest-fidelity main run.
primary.how_to_play: Play an original cabinet or a legal arcade-emulation setup with gun/pedal-style input; then use the PlayStation version for the exclusive Special mode.

secondary.exclusive_content: Special mode/add-on stages with multiple paths and endings
secondary.what_to_play: Play the PlayStation Special mode after the arcade campaign.
secondary.why: The PlayStation port adds post-story stages and branching/endings not in the arcade game.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Namco Super System 22 arcade cabinet with pedal and blowback light gun.
GunCon-supported home port with lower frame rate/polygon compromises, but exclusive Special mode/add-on stages.
all_releases.reason: secondary: play for exclusive Special mode content.

all_releases.fidelity: Japan-only PS2 release route.
all_releases.reason: skip: no unique content exists over the arcade/PlayStation split.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade has the best original fidelity and controller design; PlayStation has exclusive Special mode content but visible technical compromises.

emulation.notes: Use GunCon 2-compatible hardware if possible; otherwise calibrate a pointer/mouse setup in PCSX2.

primary.why: Time Crisis II was ported from arcade to PS2 with enhanced graphics and GunCon 2 support, while planned PlayStation and Dreamcast ports were canceled. The PS2 version is the best complete home route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 version with GunCon 2 on compatible display hardware, or use PCSX2 with a calibrated mouse/pointer setup.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Namco System 23/Super System 23 arcade release with linked co-op cabinets.
all_releases.reason: skip: original cabinet baseline, but PS2 has enhanced graphics and home GunCon 2 support.

all_releases.fidelity: Home release with enhanced graphics and GunCon 2 support.
Canceled ports.
all_releases.reason: skip: canceled and not playable release routes.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade is original and has linked-cabinet co-op; PS2 is enhanced and practical at home.

entries.title: Crisis Zone
entries.definitive_edition: Time Crisis: Crisis Zone on PS2

emulation.notes: Use PS2 emulation or original GunCon 2 hardware; the arcade cabinet remains the purist route.

primary.why: Crisis Zone is a Time Crisis spin-off that came from arcades to PS2 with improved polygon textures/details and an additional mission. The PS2 version is therefore the most complete release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 version on original hardware with GunCon 2 or in PCSX2 with calibrated pointer/mouse input.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Namco System 23 Evolution 2 arcade release with machine-gun cabinet setup.
all_releases.reason: skip: original baseline, but PS2 adds an extra mission and visual improvements.

all_releases.fidelity: Time Crisis: Crisis Zone with improved textures/details and an additional mission.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade cabinet is original, but PS2 adds content and visual improvements.

emulation.notes: Use GunCon-compatible hardware or a calibrated pointer/mouse setup.

primary.why: Project Titan is a PlayStation-only spin-off and direct sequel to the PlayStation port of the first Time Crisis, with a new multi-hiding mechanic. No other platform release is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation disc on original hardware with GunCon or in DuckStation with calibrated pointer/mouse input.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PS1-only release.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Only one documented platform route exists.

emulation.notes: Use GunCon 2-compatible hardware or calibrated pointer/mouse input.

primary.version: PS2 release with Alicia Winston content
primary.why: Time Crisis 3 was ported from arcade to PS2 with new plot elements, features, weapons, and playable Alicia Winston sections not found in the arcade release. The PS2 version is therefore the most complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 version with GunCon 2 on compatible hardware, or in PCSX2 with calibrated pointer/mouse input.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Namco System 246 arcade release.
all_releases.reason: skip: original cabinet baseline, but PS2 adds exclusive playable/story content.

all_releases.fidelity: Home release with additional plot/features/weapons and Alicia Winston playable content.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade is original; PS2 is more complete because of exclusive Alicia content and extra features.

entries.title: Time Crisis 4

emulation.emulator: Original PS3 hardware / RPCS3 if compatible
emulation.notes: GunCon 3 hardware is part of the intended PS3 experience; emulator/controller mapping should be verified first.

primary.why: Time Crisis 4 was ported from arcade to PS3 with GunCon 3 support, 480p/720p output, Arcade Mode, and an exclusive first-person shooter mode. The later Razing Storm compilation adds PlayStation Move support but removes the FPS mode, so the original PS3 release is the most complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original PS3 release with GunCon 3 if possible; use the Razing Storm compilation only if PlayStation Move support matters more than the missing FPS mode.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Namco System Super 256 arcade release.
all_releases.reason: skip: original baseline, but PS3 adds FPS mode and home display support.

all_releases.fidelity: GunCon 3 release with 480p/720p support, Arcade Mode, Crisis Missions, and exclusive FPS mode.
Compilation re-release with PlayStation Move support but without the FPS mode.
all_releases.reason: skip: useful Move route, but missing exclusive FPS mode from the original PS3 release.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Razing Storm compilation has Move support, but original PS3 release has exclusive FPS mode and is more complete.

entries.remaster_caveats: Razing Storm compilation removes the FPS mode despite adding PlayStation Move support.

entries.title: Time Crisis Strike

emulation.notes: No recommended modern storefront route is documented.

primary.why: Time Crisis Strike is a mobile spin-off of Time Crisis 3 with a different story, released for iOS and J2ME. It is a delisted/preservation-only side entry rather than a main arcade route.
primary.how_to_play: Treat this as a delisted mobile preservation entry; only use an already-owned legitimate copy or archived mobile device.

all_releases.fidelity: Mobile spin-off with touchscreen/keypad-oriented play.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Mobile availability and delisting/preservation constraints dominate the best-version decision.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or current storefront route exists.

entries.title: Razing Storm
entries.definitive_edition: Time Crisis: Razing Storm on PS3

emulation.emulator: Original PS3 hardware / RPCS3 if compatible
emulation.notes: Use Move or GunCon 3 where possible; emulator support for controller mapping should be checked.

primary.why: Razing Storm was first an arcade spin-off, but the PS3 Time Crisis: Razing Storm release adds PlayStation Move/GunCon 3 support plus Story Mode, Sentry Mode, and Online Battle Mode, with story material covering arcade cliffhangers and plot holes.
primary.how_to_play: Play Time Crisis: Razing Storm on PS3 with PlayStation Move or GunCon 3; stick to arcade mode if you only want the rail-shooter core.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Namco System 357 arcade release.
all_releases.reason: skip: original baseline, but PS3 adds story and extra modes.

all_releases.fidelity: Time Crisis: Razing Storm compilation with Move/GunCon 3 support, Story Mode, Sentry Mode, and Online Battle Mode.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade is purer for the rail-shooter, but PS3 adds the story and modes that complete the package.

entries.title: Time Crisis: Razing Storm

emulation.emulator: Original PS3 hardware / RPCS3 if compatible

primary.version: Big 3 Gun Shooting / Time Crisis: Razing Storm compilation
primary.why: This PS3 compilation bundles Razing Storm with Time Crisis 4: Arcade Ver. and Deadstorm Pirates, supports both GunCon 3 and PlayStation Move, and is the broadest Time Crisis-era home light-gun package.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PS3 with PlayStation Move or GunCon 3; use it as a compilation route rather than the definitive version of Time Crisis 4's FPS mode.

all_releases.fidelity: PS3 light-gun compilation with Razing Storm, Time Crisis 4: Arcade Ver., and Deadstorm Pirates plus Move/GunCon 3 support.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Best as a compilation; it does not replace the original Time Crisis 4 PS3 release because that release has FPS mode.

entries.remaster_caveats: Compilation version of Time Crisis 4 is Arcade Ver. and omits Time Crisis 4's FPS mode.

entries.title: Time Crisis 2nd Strike

emulation.notes: No current purchase route is documented.

primary.why: Time Crisis 2nd Strike is a mobile sequel to Time Crisis Strike and alternate-version story of Time Crisis 4, released for iOS and later Android in Japan. It supported iGunCon on iOS but is no longer available for purchase as of March 30, 2015.
primary.how_to_play: Treat this as a delisted mobile preservation entry; only use an already-owned legitimate copy/device.

all_releases.fidelity: Mobile release with iGunCon support on iOS and later Android release in Japan.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Delisting and mobile OS compatibility are the main preservation constraints.

entries.remaster_caveats: Pulled from app stores in 2015; no remaster exists.

entries.title: Time Crisis 5

emulation.notes: The two-pedal cabinet setup is part of the intended design.

primary.why: Time Crisis 5 remains arcade-only. The True Mastermind upgrade adds the second half of the game, expanding it from three stages to six, making it the complete arcade version.
primary.how_to_play: Play a cabinet running Time Crisis 5: True Mastermind; avoid the original three-stage build if you want the full game.

all_releases.fidelity: Original arcade build using two pedals.
all_releases.reason: skip: incomplete compared with True Mastermind upgrade.

all_releases.fidelity: True Mastermind edition with the second half of the game and six total stages.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Only the True Mastermind cabinet/update is complete; the earlier arcade build has half the stage count.

entries.remaster_caveats: No home port or remaster exists.
